title: asm.js: The Stepping Stone to WebAssembly
explainer: Before WebAssembly existed, Mozilla's asm.js showed that a strict, typed subset of ordinary JavaScript could be compiled ahead of time and run at near-native speed in existing browsers, with no new runtime format at all. WebAssembly's initial design deliberately reused asm.js's feature set as a starting point, so understanding why asm.js worked explains several of Wasm's early design choices.

title: Native Client: The Sandboxed-Native-Code Experiment Wasm Replaced
explainer: Years before WebAssembly, Google's Native Client, announced in 2008 and generally available in Chrome by 2011, and its portable successor PNaCl let web pages run sandboxed C/C++ code at near-native speed, but only in Chrome. In May 2017 Google announced it would deprecate PNaCl in favor of WebAssembly, which solved the same problem, near-native speed in the browser, as an open, cross-vendor standard instead of a single-browser extension.
